_note: ILLUSTRATIVE go/no-go criteria for the decision summary (task A-12, revised in A-15 after the 12 Oct 2026 review, C-10: no cost or competitor criteria; completeness, compliance and schedule come from the units' validated answers). Thresholds are PLACEHOLDERS to be agreed with the bid manager. Layer 0 gives advice; the bid manager decides.

criteria.name: Assessment complete
criteria.question: Has every item sent to the units been answered and validated?

criteria.name: Compliance
criteria.question: Are enough product requirements fully or partially compliant in the validated answers (at least the compliance threshold)?

criteria.name: Schedule
criteria.question: Can the units meet the RFP's dates?

criteria.name: Scope fit
criteria.question: Do the suggested units fit the RFP's scope (no unit outside the layers the RFP covers)?

criteria.name: Every requirement routed
criteria.question: Does every requirement in the published register have an owner (a participating unit, the bid desk (commercial and submission items) for non-product items, or a recorded capability gap)?

criteria.name: Open questions
criteria.question: Are there no open questions (rule warnings, requirements with source not verified, questions not yet closed)?

criteria.name: No pending-acquisition dependency
criteria.question: Does nothing depend on a unit whose acquisition has not closed (EPC Power)?

criteria.name: Deviations from the standard product
criteria.question: Does the RFP's data sheet stay within the standard ratings of the products offered?

criteria.name: Capacity and portfolio conflicts
criteria.question: Do the units have capacity for this work, given their open work on other bids?

preliminary_feasibility._note: P-38 (C-23): the overall assessment score, a PLACEHOLDER formula to be agreed with the bid manager. It is a count of requirements, never a probability; retrieval scores and model confidence are not part of it.
preliminary_feasibility.formula: Of the technical requirements (categories technical and compliance): a requirement with validated unit answers counts as feasible when every validated answer is fully or partially compliant; one without counts as feasible when it is matched to a unit's product (domain alignment) and the latest assessment run found reviewed product evidence for it. Preliminary feasibility = feasible / technical requirements.
